divider.title: The Brand Meaning Ladder
divider.subtitle: A simple way to understand how consumers see a brand - from what it is and does, to what it means to them
divider.direction: From functional benefits → to emotions → to values and purpose.

placement.headline: Levels of branding: where the category is, and where PTCL is talking
placement.standfirst: Each brand sits on the level most of its coded posts occupy (mean level in brackets). Placement computed from the classified posts, not asserted.

rows.name: Human values / way of life
rows.note: Stated only in one-off CSR posts; no brand's communication lives here.

rows.name: Psychological territory
rows.note: Transworld, Ufone - household truths, nostalgia, relatability (not yet classified post by post).

rows.name: Product benefits
rows.note: Tapmad, Multinet, Jazz Business - problem-led, what it does for you (not yet classified post by post).

rows.name: Product attributes
rows.note: StormFiber, Zong, Optix, Jazz - speed, price and coverage tiles (not yet classified post by post).

rows.name: Name only
rows.note: heritage as recognition (79 years, national days) plus pride through hockey and esports.

placement.conclusion: PTCL talks in recognition and national pride while customers judge the category on benefits - and the ladder does not let a brand skip the rungs between.
placement.footnote: Framework: Brand Meaning Ladder. Placement = modal level across each brand's classified posts; mean in brackets (ladder_levels.csv). Competitor rows are descriptive until their posts are classified.

factor_list.headline: The Brand Meaning Ladder for fixed broadband: the factors at each level
factor_list.standfirst: Current = seen in the category's 336 posts.  Potential = relevant to connectivity, not yet claimed.  Unsupported = little link to connectivity.  † = added for this category.

rows.name: Purpose / philosophy
current: No clear purpose evidence in the category
potential: Empowering people to create a better future
Changing the way people think about a category

factor_list.conclusion: Current factors cluster at levels 1-3. The unclaimed territory sits at levels 4-6 - but higher is not better: a factor is only worth owning if it is relevant, credible, distinctive and defensible.
factor_list.footnote: Framework: Brand Meaning Ladder - factor lists per level. Current factors: 336 coded Instagram posts, 14 brands (codes.csv). † additions: category scan and consumer conversation analysis.

category_evidence.headline: How the Brand Meaning Ladder works in fixed broadband
category_evidence.standfirst: The factors that populate each level in this category - from 336 competitor posts and 976 customer comments. Levels are depth of meaning, not stages: higher is not better.

rows.name: Purpose / philosophy
rows.brands_claim: No brand states a purpose. Social work appears as one-off CSR and awareness-day posts, not as a reason the brand exists.
rows.customers_judge: Not raised as purpose. Unequal access surfaces only as a complaint: "there is no other provider here".
rows.open: Digital inclusion; connecting village to city; enabling livelihoods.

rows.name: Values / way of life
rows.brands_claim: National development and social responsibility, mostly through national days and CSR. Few posts state an actual belief.
rows.customers_judge: Whether they are dealt with straight - claims, packages and bills that match what they get.
rows.open: Fairness and straight dealing; inclusion; progress; togetherness.

rows.name: Psychological
rows.brands_claim: Pride through sport and celebrity (hockey, esports); nostalgia and belonging (Ufone, Transworld's 1947); modern and aspirational (devices 14, innovation 12); gamer identity (10).
rows.customers_judge: Smart choice ("more speed for less"); respected when answered; trapped when there is "no option".
rows.open: In control; respected as a customer; confident, smart chooser.

rows.name: Benefits
rows.brands_claim: Business keeps running (50: Multinet 20, Jazz Business 16, Wateen 13); entertainment at home (49: Tapmad 23, Shoq 14); value for money (31: Zong 9, Optix 7); help when needed (15); fewer disruptions (8).
rows.customers_judge: Work, study and stream without breaks; a fault fixed quickly; a bill that stays predictable.
rows.open: A bill that does not change without notice; a fault fixed without pleading; a clean exit.

rows.name: Attributes
rows.brands_claim: Price, packages and bundles (31); devices (14: Jazz 7, PTCL 4); coverage and new areas (11: StormFiber 9); speed and fibre (11: Nayatel 4, Optix 3).
rows.customers_judge: Mbps delivered versus Mbps sold; the actual monthly bill; availability on my street.
rows.open: Proof - 0 of 336 posts cite a speed test; published price terms; a published fault-response time.

rows.name: Identification
rows.brands_claim: Name, logo and distinctive assets; heritage and national days (59 posts, 13 of 14 brands); sponsorships and awards; corporate announcements (61).
rows.customers_judge: Which brands people name when they shop: PTCL 92, Ufone 89, Jazz 41, Zong 35, StormFiber 13 mentions.
rows.open: Table stakes - every brand is already past this level.

category_evidence.conclusion: The category talks at levels 1-3 - who we are, what we have, what you can watch or run. Nobody makes the relationship itself a benefit, and that is where customers judge hardest.
category_evidence.footnote: Framework: Brand Meaning Ladder. Counts = posts whose main claim is that factor, of 336 (codes.csv); a claim can sit at more than one level, so counts show where factors appear, not per-level totals.

client_ladder.headline: {client}'s Brand Meaning Ladder: the category's factors, and where to stand
client_ladder.standfirst: {client} says = its {n} coded posts, classified by level (mode L{mode}, mean {mean:.1f}). Heard = 976 YouTube comments. Higher is not better - the target is the deepest level {client} can prove.

rows.name: Purpose / philosophy
rows.in_use: None - no brand states a purpose in 336 posts.
rows.open: Connecting every Pakistani home, village to city, on fair terms (opportunity only).

rows.name: Values / way of life
rows.open: Fairness and straight dealing; equal access for villages.

rows.name: Psychological
rows.in_use: National pride via sport and celebrity; aspiration and modernity; belonging and nostalgia (Transworld, Ufone).
rows.open: Being in control; being respected as a customer; the smart choice.

rows.name: Benefits
rows.in_use: Entertainment at home (49); business continuity (50); value for money (31); help when needed (15).
rows.open: A bill that does not change without notice; a fault fixed without pleading; a clean exit.
rows.heard: Weak - it works "if your location is good".
rows.placement_sub: fair terms you can count on

rows.name: Attributes
rows.in_use: Price and bundles (31); device bundles (14); speed tiers (11); coverage and new areas (11).
rows.open: Proof - 0 posts cite a speed test; a published fault-response time; published price terms.
rows.heard: Mixed - 100+ Mbps where good; speed below package, bills rising.

rows.name: Identification
rows.in_use: Name, logo, heritage and national days (59 posts, 13 of 14 brands); sponsorships.
rows.open: Table stakes - nothing left to claim.
rows.heard: Strong - most-mentioned brand; Flash Fiber asked for by name.

client_ladder.conclusion: Place PTCL at Level 3: fair terms you can count on. Nobody in the category claims it, it answers the customer pulse directly, and PTCL can prove it with commercial decisions. Level 4 is earned from there.
client_ladder.footnote: Framework: Brand Meaning Ladder. PTCL levels: ptcl_ladder_levels.csv (hand-classified). Consumer evidence: 976 YouTube comments - self-selected corpus, not a satisfaction measure.
